skip: The saved article (Taxiles) has under 300 words of substance, most of which the existing description already gives (submission to Alexander, rivalry with Porus, troops for the Hydaspes). What it adds would fill one short paragraph: the embassy sent while Alexander was in Sogdiana, the gifts exchanged (200 talents of silver, 3,000 oxen, 10,000 sheep; in return Persian robes, 30 horses and 1,000 talents in gold), help to Hephaestion and Perdiccas in bridging the Indus at Hund, 5,000 men at the Hydaspes, and that Eudemus later took over Taxila briefly. The article dates him r. 326-316 BCE and Alexander's first descent into India to 327 BCE.
